name: How do you choose the right room sizes in a custom plan?

mainEntity.name: What is the best way to decide bedroom, kitchen, and living room sizes in a custom floor plan?
mainEntity.text: What is the best way to decide bedroom, kitchen, and living room sizes in a custom floor plan?

acceptedAnswer.text: The right room sizes come from function, furniture, and flow, not from guessing or copying another home. A bedroom should comfortably fit the intended bed, circulation space, and storage. A kitchen should reflect how often the household cooks and whether it needs an island, pantry, prep zones, or multiple users at once. Living areas should be sized for the number of people who will use them regularly, not just for occasional entertaining. In custom floor-plan development, it helps to prioritize the rooms that matter most and avoid giving every space equal weight. A home feels better when important rooms are generous and secondary areas are efficient. Overly large rooms can create wasted square footage and raise construction costs without improving livability. The best designers use furniture plans, lifestyle questions, and budget limits to balance comfort and efficiency.
acceptedAnswer.description: Room sizes should be based on how the spaces will actually be used, furniture needs, circulation, and the overall budget. Oversized rooms can waste square footage, while undersized rooms can make the home feel cramped and reduce function.
